newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends 71 cts down on heavy profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends 71 cts down on heavy profit-taking.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures shed 71 cents on Thursday to end at a session low of $18.17 after traders grabbed profits and baled out of the market ahead of the long holiday weekend in the United States.
"A lot of people went long yesterday and they just wanted to get out of their positions," said one broker. "A lot of locals in the States were very big sellers."
The Brent contract closed early at 1705 GMT in line with the early close of trade on NYMEX for Independence Day holidays.
U.S. markets will not reopen until Monday.
July gas oil closed slightly earlier $3.00 a tonne down at $164.50, just 25 cents off the day's low.

News that Iraq had completed its aid hand-out plan under the U.N. food-for-oil deal encouraged the sell-off, but in any case traders were keen to cash in after four straight days of gains on the oil market.

"There's a feeling that there might be some more progress on Iraq over the weekend so no-one wants to be left long," a broker said. "But anyway they were able to take some nice profits and flush a few of the stops out."

Iraq's United Nations co-ordinator said on Thursday that Baghdad and the U.N. have completed their aid distribution plans to cover the next six months of oil exports and would send it to the U.N. for approval soon.
Finalisation of the plan is the next step towards a resumption of oil sales.
